  "text": "The gate settled into its frame with a sound like a door closing in an empty house. Mara’s father let go of the wheel. Across the glass, the seven lights dwindled until only darkness remained.

“Who were they?” Mara asked.

The woman in the ship’s coat did not answer. She was watching the lantern on the sill. Its flame had turned blue.

Above them, the harbor master called that the waterline was dropping. Boots sounded on the stairs, then stopped. He had seen the lantern too.

“It came through the gate?” he asked.

Mara nodded.

He took off his cap and held it against his chest. “There was a boat lost out there,” he said. “The winter they sealed the old passage. Seven aboard.”

The woman stepped away from the glass. “Eight,” she said. “My father went after them.”

A faint knock came from the pipe: two, then one. She put her palm against the wall, but no second signal followed.

Mara looked at the bell lodged against the grate. When she pulled it free, water poured from its mouth. On the brass, beneath a crust of silt, someone had scratched a name. She carried it to the woman.

For a long time, the woman held the bell without speaking. Then she gave it one gentle shake. Its note traveled down the pipe, clear and small.

The lantern flame bent toward the flooded passage. Far beyond the glass, a single light answered. It hovered there until the woman raised her hand. Then it turned and followed the others into the dark."
